title: How the Gambit Got Its Name
body: In his early chess writings, Ruy Lopez introduced the word "gambit" to describe a sneaky way of playing. He borrowed the term from Italian to explain a strategy based on tricks, traps, and sacrifices. He used these new ideas to defeat older masters who did not yet understand how fast the game had become.

variants.lucy: Long ago, a writer named Ruy López wrote down a beautiful new word for a clever way to play. He borrowed the term "gambit" from the Italian language to describe a quiet trap. By offering a small piece as a gift, a player could lure their opponent into a surprise.
variants.luca: This was a daring plan built for speed and surprise! Ruy used these clever sacrifices to challenge the older masters who were used to a much slower game. His lightning-fast tricks caught them completely off guard, changing how the game was played forever.

source.book: The Art of the Game of Chess
source.author: Ruy López, trans. Andrew Soltis & Michael J. McGrath
